issues.failure_explanation: The stationarity condition at $\bar w$ involves the rank-based probabilities $p_i(\bar w)$, but the proof substitutes the probabilities $p_i(w_C)$ of an unrelated point $w_C=C\bar w$ — an invalid inference; the claim that the equality region of two quadratics is a halfspace is false (it is an Apollonius sphere), and the 'repeat recursively' extension and the 'results hold irrespective of that' assertion are unproven. Moreover the stated sufficient condition is too weak: it is built on $\theta_{M,\bar w}=\max_i\theta_{i,\bar w}$ (the worst-aligned outlier), while the binding clean/outlier crossing toward $\bar w$ is governed by the best-aligned outlier. Counterexample: clean samples $f_i(w)=\|w\|^2$, outlier A $=100\|w-2.1u\|^2$, outlier B $=\|w-10u_B\|^2$ with $\angle(u,u_B)\approx88.9^\circ$, $\delta=1$, $\gamma=2/10=0.2$, $\kappa=100$, $k\approx0.15n$ (so $\hat p_{\max}=p_{m_1}+p_{m_2}\approx0.278$). Then $q=(\cos\theta_M/\gamma)(1+\sqrt\kappa)-1\approx0.012>0$ and $\hat p_{\max}\le1/(1+\kappa q)\approx0.455$, so both hypotheses hold; yet $\bar w=\frac{p_A\cdot100\cdot2.1}{p_A\cdot100+0.85}u\approx1.99u$ is a self-consistent stationary point (outlier A has the lowest loss there, $p_A=0.15$, B is last-ranked) lying beyond the clean/A crossing $(10/11)\cdot2.1\approx1.91$, so $f_A(\bar w)<f_i(\bar w)$ for all clean $i$ and $\bar w\notin\mathcal B_r(\ws)$.

issues.failure_explanation: In eq:contraction, Term1 enters with a negative coefficient $-2\eta_t(1-\eta_t\sup_iL_i)$, so upper-bounding Term1 cannot upper-bound the expectation. The needed (and true) bound is the reverse: $Term1=\sum_{i\in\mathcal G}p_i\langle w_t-\wg,\nabla f_i(w_t)-\nabla f_i(\wg)\rangle\ge\min_{i\in\mathcal G}p_i\cdot|\mathcal G|\lambda_{good}\|w_t-\wg\|^2$, by monotonicity of each $f_i$ and strong convexity of $F_{good}$. As written, the chain asserts 'Term1 $\le$ …' (the false direction for nonnegative summands with $p_i\ge\min p_i$), evaluates the norm at $w_{t+1}$ instead of $w_t$, and drops the factor $|\mathcal G|$; the proof as written therefore does not establish the stated contraction factor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the rest of the paper, we will focus on the ``with replacement'' scenario for ease of presentation; this choice does not change our main ideas or results.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims a clean dichotomy: $k\ge n\epsilon+1$ gives exact consistency, and 'in all other cases' a non-zero outlier contribution prevents it. Under the with-replacement sampling the paper declares as its focus, every sample has positive pick probability (the worst-ranked sample has probability $1/n^k>0$), so near $\ws$ the outlier gradients contribute $\sum_{j\in\mathbb O}p_j\nabla f_j\neq0$ generically and $\ws$ is not a stationary point; the best established guarantee is $\|\wsm-\ws\|\le\epsilon^kG/\lambda>0$ for every finite $k$. The threshold $k\ge|\mathbb O|+1$ yields exactly zero outlier probability only under without-replacement sampling (where the bottom $|\mathbb O|$ ranks have probability zero for $k>|\mathbb O|$), a model the paper said it would not focus on (though the appendix corollary uses its probability formula).
